summary:
MarsBase AI is an interactive educational simulation where users become the mission commander of a fictional Mars base called Ares. Over seven sols (Martian days), players manage a four-person crew by balancing energy, oxygen, water, and food resources while operating five interconnected base systems: solar panels, an oxygen plant, a water recycler, a greenhouse, and a radiation shelter.

Each sol presents a unique scenario inspired by real NASA research — from dust storms reducing solar output (inspired by InSight) to water filter failures (inspired by ECLSS) and solar particle radiation events (inspired by Orion crew protection). Players must make strategic decisions, allocate limited resources, and complete at least three of five engineering objectives to succeed.

The application features an interactive 3D Mars base built with Three.js, real-time NASA DONKI space weather telemetry integration, bilingual support (English/Turkish), an optional AI-powered mission advisor, and a built-in science library linking every game mechanic to its NASA source. MarsBase AI transforms complex space engineering concepts into an engaging, accessible learning experience for young explorers.
details:
What it does: MarsBase AI is a browser-based Mars base survival training simulation. Players take command of a four-person crew at the fictional Ares Mars Base, managing interconnected life-support systems across seven sols. The game uses a deterministic resource engine where every decision has traceable, quantifiable consequences — no randomness in resolution, only in mission variant selection.

How it works:

  • Resource Management Engine: A pure, deterministic TypeScript engine calculates energy production (solar panels), oxygen generation (CO₂ conversion plant inspired by MOXIE), water recycling (inspired by ECLSS), food production (greenhouse with scheduled harvests), and crew life support costs each sol. Resources are scored 0–100 points.
  • Event System: Seven themed sols present real challenges: Sol 1 activates life support, Sol 2 balances harvest with storm preparation, Sol 3 simulates a dust storm cutting solar to 25%, Sol 4 introduces a water filter failure at 40% efficiency, Sol 5 triggers a solar particle radiation event requiring shelter, Sol 6 is the final harvest window, and Sol 7 is base handover.
  • Interactive 3D Scene: A fully procedural Three.js scene renders the Mars base with terrain, sky, habitat modules, solar arrays, greenhouse, water plant, oxygen tanks, observatory, and animated astronauts — all generated at runtime from code, no external 3D model files.
  • NASA Data Integration: The server fetches real-time data from NASA's DONKI API (solar flares, solar energetic particle events) and NASA Image Library (Mars surface images from Curiosity), cached hourly, with graceful fallback to offline data.
  • AI Mission Advisor: An optional AI advisor (NVIDIA Nemotron or OpenRouter) receives the current game state, the player's draft plan, engine predictions, lesson context, and NASA telemetry to provide contextual guidance. Without an API key, a local rule-based diagnostic system operates fully offline.
  • Science Library: Nine science fact cards link every game mechanic to published NASA resources (MOXIE, ECLSS, InSight dust storm data, Orion crew systems, Mars24 sol calculations, space radiation hazards, and plant biology experiments).
  • Bilingual Support: Full English and Turkish localization for all UI text, lessons, science content, events, and advisor responses.

Tools and technologies: TypeScript, React 19, Vite 7, Three.js, Framer Motion, Lucide React icons, Node.js server with Vite plugin middleware, NASA DONKI API, NASA Image Library API, Vitest + Testing Library + Playwright for testing, Inter and Space Grotesk fonts (SIL OFL).

Intended impact: Make complex space engineering trade-offs — energy budgeting, life support cascading failures, radiation protection — intuitive and engaging for young learners. Every game mechanic is transparently connected to its NASA science source, encouraging curiosity-driven exploration of real space research.
